summary: Steel-frame fire lookout on Black Mountain, Kentucky's highest point, in Harlan County; cab gone by 2008; access rule and current owner conflict across sources.

facts.design: Steel frame tower; cab and lowest flight of stairs removed
facts.status_note: Cab removed and lower stairs gone; steel frame remains per 2008 visit report. Wikipedia calls it abandoned
facts.agency: Penn Virginia Coal Company (administrator per NHLR); Wikipedia says the Commonwealth of Kentucky now owns the land

access.note: NHLR says a liability release is required to visit; Wikipedia says no waiver is now needed, undated. Unresolved

events.note: Visit report 28 Sep 2008: cab in pieces on the ground, stairs rotten and first run missing, steel frame good, concrete foundations cracked; not staffed

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR names Penn Virginia Coal Company as administrator; Wikipedia says a Penn Virginia company (Penn Virginia Resources, Radnor PA) formerly owned the summit and that Kentucky now owns the land. Story gives both and does not settle the current owner.

notes_for_editor: No build date or builder found in any source read. Access and current owner conflict: NHLR (2014 listing) requires a liability release; Wikipedia (undated) says Kentucky owns the land and no waiver is needed. The waiver notice Wikipedia cites (a 2010 highpointers.org item) could not be read: the PDF link in the brief returned 404 and the source is not in the cache, so the Wikipedia change is unconfirmed. The brief's company name (Penn Virginia Coal Company) and Wikipedia's (Penn Virginia Resources) differ; both are reported. NHLR elevation 1,263 m matches the record. Electronics encroachment on the tower is noted in the 2008 visit. A separate planned overlook tower near Black Mountain (seen in search snippets only) is not the historic lookout and is not used. No photos added.
